agent_notes: No previous verse in the packet (GEN.37.36 is outside the window), so the dramatic voice opens fresh, with the sold-Joseph backdrop only implied by 'went down'. The chapter's placement and its dating ('at that time') are disputed: Ibn Ezra says the events precede Joseph's sale; Rashi and Radak read it as after. I translated 'at that time' neutrally and did not take a side.
STEPBible glosses vayyamet as 'and he put to death' (Hiphil). Literal layer keeps the causative: 'and he caused him to die'. KJV 'slew' is acceptable but the Hebrew has no violence word.

Revised per request. The 'putting her off with a straw' reading is Rashi's alone (citing Ketubot 43 for the presumption that a woman whose husbands die will bury more). Ramban quotes Rashi and rejects it: in his view Judah meant to wait because Shelah was still a boy. Radak (Genesis Rabbah 85:5, Rabbi Eleazar) treats the fear as a sign even without augury. Gloss for שבי: STEPBible 'dwell', changed to 'remain' in context; אלמנה is a predicate 'as a widow'. Ramban's remark on mourning garments is his inference and stays out of the translation.

(GEN.38.11: "for he said, Lest peradventure he die also, as his brethren did"; Ramban on 38:11 quotes Rashi ("דוחה היה אותה בקש... לשון רש"י"), then: "ולא ידעתי למה יתבייש יהודה... והנכון בעיני שהיה שלה ראוי ליבם, אבל לא רצה אביו שייבם אותה ועודנו נער")

agent_notes: Dating: the verse has no dating formula beyond 'the days multiplied'; Radak cites Genesis Rabbah for 'twelve months', which I did not repeat as fact. 'Went up' (ויעל) vs Samson's 'went down' to Timnah (Radak) reflects the vantage point of each traveler. The chapter's ledger event has Judah 'comforted' as a separate clause from the shearing trip.

בפתח עינים: STEPBible and Ibn Ezra take Enaim as a place name; Rashi, Rashbam and Sforno read 'at the opening of the eyes/springs', a crossroads. I gloss it as the place name 'Enaim' and keep the pun on 'opening/eyes' only in the commentary; the Hebrew preposition pattern in 38.21 (בָעֵינַיִם, with the article-like vocalization) is what Rashbam argues from, and I report it as his argument rather than settle it.
וַתִּתְעַלָּף: the packet gloss 'wrapped herself up' kept. Ibn Ezra ties it to Jonah 4:8 (hiding the face); Radak reads 'in fine clothes'. I follow Ibn Ezra and Rashbam (covered, concealed).

The KJV 'harlot' renders זונה; in 38.21-22 the text switches to קדשה. The five English versions flatten both to 'harlot/prostitute'; STEPBible glosses קדשה 'cult prostitute'. I keep the Hebrew's two words distinct in the literal layer ('prostitute' vs 'consecrated woman') and argue in the commentary that the shift is Hirah's courtesy, not a second profession. The sacral-prostitution reading of qedeshah is itself disputed in modern scholarship; I flag it rather than assert it.

פתילך: 'cord' (ASV, YLT 'ribbon') against KJV 'bracelets'. Ramban objects to Rashi's 'garment' and the plural at 38.25. I gloss it 'cord' and cite Ramban, Radak and Rashbam for the competing readings. The KJV 'bracelets' has no basis in the Hebrew singular.

'Canaanite' as 'merchant' (Onkelos, Rashi, Ramban, Radak) is a Targumic reading; I keep the literal gentilic in the translation and mention the merchant reading in the commentary. The daughter's own name is never given; she appears only as 'daughter of Shua' (confirmed in v.12).

The Hebrew names no person called Hirah in this verse: it says 'his friend the Adullamite'. BBE supplies 'Hirah' from 38.12. Our packet's prior verse names Hirah, so the dramatic layer may use it as continuity; the literal layer does not.

Radak and Ramban give the burning-penalty rationale as a status-of-the-betrothed (shomeret yavam) argument; Rashi cites a rabbinic tradition that Tamar was a priest's daughter (Shem). I cite them as the commentators' views, not as the plain sense. I could not source the claim that burning was a Canaanite or patriarchal-era penalty independently of these, so the commentary keeps it in the voice of 'the narrative assumes'.
כמשלש חדשים: 'about three months' per all five versions; Rashi and Radak cite Genesis Rabbah 85 for pregnancy being noticeable at three months. Kept as a note, not a claim of my own.

STEPBible glosses אֵלֶּה לּוֹ as 'belong to him'; I kept 'are his' since Hebrew has only the dative 'to him'. 'Cords' (plural פְּתִילִים) is rendered as a plain plural; KJV 'bracelets' is not supported by the word's other uses (e.g. Num 19:15 and Judg 16:9 use pathil for a cord or thread). That the seal hung on the cord is my reading of the verse, not stated in it.

הִיא מוּצֵאת is a passive participle: 'she is being brought out' (Ibn Ezra notes the unusual form with the aleph kept). Rashi, Radak and Sforno all read her silence about Judah's name as deliberate; I cite them and do not claim it as my own.

צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי can mean 'she is more in the right than I' (comparative min, as Rashbam, Ramban and Radak read it, with parallels in 1 Sam 24:18 and 1 Kgs 2:32) or Rashi's 'from me [she is pregnant]'. I took the comparative as the plain sense and gave the other in the commentary. The five English versions agree on the comparative.
וְלֹא־יָסַף: Rashi and Ramban record both 'did not do it again' and 'did not cease'. I kept the plain 'did not add again' and left the dispute to the commentary.

Addressed the reviewer request: the literal layer now keeps the repeated root (breached a breach) and the exclamatory turn of מה, and renders עליך as 'upon yourself'. The KJV audit no longer faults 'upon thee'; it faults the lost root play and the 'How...?' question.

Meaning of עליך is disputed. Rashi/Ramban: a breach made upon himself, as of a fence that closed round him. Ibn Ezra and Radak: the breach is a liability that rests on you. Ramban calls Ibn Ezra's reading pointless. I keep 'upon yourself' literal, which allows both.

Subject of וַיִּקְרָא is unmarked ('someone called'). Radak says Judah; I keep it impersonal in the literal layer and in the dramatic layer. STEPBible has the last פָּרֶץ as the name (H6557) and the first as the common noun (H6556).
The speaker is the midwife per Radak; the text says only 'she said'. The dramatic layer keeps 'the midwife' to continue verse 28.

agent_notes: The verb 'was' in 'and he was in Kezib' has Judah as its most natural subject (Rashbam), though the grammar is ambiguous (Ramban discusses alternatives). The place name כזיב echoes the root כזב 'to deceive, fail' (Rashi, citing Jer 15:18); I treat that as a possible wordplay, not a certainty.

יבם is a denominative verb built on יָבָם 'husband's brother'; there is no exact English verb. STEPBible's 'act as a husband's brother for' is kept. The 'seed' (זרע) here means offspring, as the five English versions agree.

Revised per request. 'Not his' is read as 'would not be called by his name' on the authority of Ibn Ezra (citing Deut 25:6) and the two Targums (Onkelos: 'seed is not called by his name'; Pseudo-Jonathan: 'children were not called by his name'). I removed the inheritance-of-the-firstborn motive: neither the verse nor these commentators state it, and it appears in the commentary only as a flagged inference. Sforno gives a different motive (the brother would gain merit through him) and I report it as his. 'Spoiled' for שחת stays; the withdrawal reading is Rashi's (quoting Genesis Rabbah) and Radak's, and Ibn Ezra rejects Ben Tamim's alternative. Note: the 'Stakes for actors' line in the locked v8 still says Onan stands to inherit the firstborn's share; v8 is approved, so I did not touch it, but it should be reopened to match this verse.

agent_notes: Слово петилеха переведено «шнур», как в английском слое; Синодальный даёт «перевязь». В комментарии отмечено, что Синодальный выбор отличается от KJV «браслеты», но тоже не «шнур».
Синодальный перевод пишет «Хананеянин»; в литературном слое оставлено «хананеянин» (родовое слово), а возможное чтение «купец» (Таргум) сохранено в примечании.

Кедеша переведено «посвящённая» в буквальном слое и «святая женщина» в литературном; в Синодальном стоит «блудница» в обоих стихах (15 и 21), так что смена регистра там скрыта. Это отмечено в комментарии.
Глагол «зна» (впала в блуд) и существительное «зенуним» — один корень; в русском «впала в блуд» / «от блуда» это сохраняет.
מַטֶּה везде «трость», как в ст. 18 и в Синодальном переводе; «перевязь» Синодального описана как не украшение (KJV) и не шнур. מוּצֵאת передано «Её выводили».

history.note: [should_fix] Use «трость» for מַטֶּה in the literal, dramatic, gloss 20 and the commentary, as in v18. Optionally render מוּצֵאת more naturally: «Её выводили» instead of «Она [была] выводима». (GEN.38.25: הַחֹתֶמֶת וְהַפְּתִילִים וְהַמַּטֶּה; GEN.38.18 (RusSynodal and ru literal): «трость твою»; RusSynodal 38:25 «печать и перевязь и трость»; ru v18 commentary: «он ближе к «одежде», чем к «шнуру»».)

agent_notes: צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי: Синодальный «она правее меня». В буквальном слое «она права, более чем я», в драматическом «она права больше, чем я»; юридический оттенок «право» вместо «праведности» объяснён в комментарии.
שָׁנִי: «багряная нить»; Синодальный «красная нить». В комментарии оговорено, что это дорогая краска из кермеса.

Игра פָּרַצְתָּ… פָּרֶץ: в буквальном слое «ты проломил… пролом»; в драматическом «какой пролом… ты пробил», чтобы слышался корень в имени Фарес. Синодальный «расторг себе преграду» и «Фарес» указаны в комментарии.
Имя Зара (Синодальный) сохранено; «Заря-Алая» в драматическом слое передаёт английское «Dawn-Red» как объяснение рабби, а не текста: оно подано в виде приложения, как в английском.

Везде «Хезив» по Синодальному переводу и по сущности loc.achzib. «Кезив» упомянут один раз в комментарии, как транслитерация еврейского כזיב, чтобы была слышна игра слов. В Мих 1:14 Синодальный пишет «Ахзив» — оставлено в скобках.

history.note: [should_fix] Use «Хезив» (в Хезиве) in the literal and dramatic layers, gloss 10, the commentary and the note on בִכְזִיב; mention «Кезив» only once, as the transliteration of the Hebrew, if the wordplay needs it. (GEN.38.5 (RusSynodal): "Иуда был в Хезиве, когда она родила его"; entity.ru:loc.achzib canonical_name «Хезив»; event.ru:evt.gen_38.shelah_born «в Хезиве».)

agent_notes: Божье имя: в буквальном слое остаётся YHWH, в драматическом — «Господь», как в Синодальном переводе.
Для глагола וְיַבֵּם выбрано «исполни долг деверя» (Синодальный: «женись на ней, как деверь»); в комментарии отмечено, что цель — родить ребёнка, а не взять жену.

Эвфемизм «и погубил на землю» передан в буквальном слое близко к еврейскому («погубил [это] на землю»); в драматическом слое выбрано «дал ему пропасть на земле». Синодальное «изливал семя» уточняет то, что в иврите не названо; об этом сказано в комментарии.

history.note: [consider] Write «Форма в иврите обозначает повторяемость («было, если входил…»)». (GEN.38.9: וְהָיָה אִם־בָּא; en: "The Hebrew is habitual".)

[event:evt.gen_38.er_marries_tamar] The 22 years from the sale (Joseph 17) to the descent (Joseph 39) are tight for: Er's birth, marriage at about 13, Onan's act, Shelah grown, Perez born and, by Gen 46:12, Perez's sons Hezron and Hamul. My chain puts Perez's birth about 19 years after the sale, so those sons must be counted in Egypt or 'born' loosely (Ibn Ezra). I kept the chain and flag the tension. The Chronologist for GEN.46 should compare.
[event:evt.gen_38.tamar_pregnancy_reported] v24 'about three months' is counted from the union (the conception), not from the pledge search. Rashi's reading is a bit over two months; margin 3 weeks.
[event:evt.gen_38.twins_born] The birth is dated by gestation (9 months from the conception), not by the text, which only says 'in the time of her travail'.

[event:evt.gen_38.kid_sent_with_hirah] The text gives no interval between the encounter and the sending. I assumed Judah stayed through the shearing at Timnah for a few days, and Hirah walks Timnah to Enaim with the kid.
[event:evt.gen_38.shelah_born] Chezib = Achzib (loc.achzib); the text says only that Judah (or Shelah, the Hebrew subject is ambiguous) was there.
[event:evt.gen_38.judah_marries_shua] Pseudo-Jonathan says Judah converted her; not used for dating.

[entity:person.daughter_of_shua] The text never names Judah's first wife; she is 'the daughter of Shua'. I made her a separate entity with null tipnr_id and kept person.shua (the TIPNR individual) as a mentioned father. TIPNR's note says Shua is the Canaanite father.
[entity:person.perez] first_mention_verse is GEN.38.27 (the twins) rather than 38.29, where the name appears; the registry lists the name only at 38.29, so the verse check may warn.
[entity:person.zerah] Same as Perez: first_mention_verse is set to the twins' verse (38.27), the name appears at 38.30.

[entity:person.midwife_of_tamar] Unnamed midwife defined as an entity because she acts (ties the thread, speaks at the birth). In GEN.38.29 the Hebrew 'she said' has the midwife as subject by context.
[event_links:evt.gen_38.hand_out_scarlet_thread] The text does not say which twin put out the hand until 38:30; I linked Zerah here by hindsight.

[event_links:evt.gen_38.er_marries_tamar] Places left out for events 38:6–11 (marriage, Er's death, Onan, Tamar's return home) and 38:12 (Shua's daughter dies), 38:19 and 38:20, 38:23–38:30 because the text does not name or imply a location. Tamar's father's house is named only as a dwelling, not a place with an identity.

[event_links:evt.gen_38.judah_goes_up_to_timnah] Timnah here is the Judean hill town (Josh 15:57), not the Dan/Philistine Timnah of Judges 14; the registry merges them in one entry. The place is the destination of the trip, so the event sits there although the text only says Judah went up to it.

[entity:loc.enaim] Enaim is probably a place-name ('two springs'), but the Hebrew can be read 'the opening of the eyes' / an open place (so KJV 'open place'). TIPNR treats it as a place; I follow it. Exact location unknown to me and no coordinates are given by the registry confirmed by me.
[entity:loc.achzib] The registry offers Achzib / Akzib / Chezib; I take Chezib of Gen 38:5 as the Judahite Achzib (Josh 15:44; Mic 1:14), not the coastal Achzib of Asher.
[entity:person.shelah.gen_38_5] Kept the registry's suffixed id because Shelah is a common name; TIPNR gives him a unique entry here.

[component:comp.judah.dwelling.1] Inferred: the text says Judah 'turned aside to' Hirah and later 'saw there' a Canaanite's daughter, so I treat him as settled near Adullam. It never closes in this chapter.

[component:comp.judahs_pledge.holder.2] Inferred: Tamar sends the items to Judah (38:25) and he recognises them (38:26); the text does not say who keeps them afterwards. I opened holder.2 at 38:25 with Judah as the holder.
[component:comp.tamar.pregnancy.1] Opened at 38:18 ('she conceived'); closed at Zerah's birth in the last event since the pregnancy ends when both twins are born.

[system:sys.levirate_marriage] Defined here, not reused. The custom is not named in the text; I name it from the behaviour (Judah's order) and Deut 25:5–10. Sheep shearing, pledge and burning are likewise new systems defined in this chapter.
[system:sys.penalty_of_burning] The text gives only the sentence ('bring her out and let her be burned'); I define the practice from it and later Israelite law, which is later than the narrative.

[event_links:evt.gen_38.hirah_asks_at_enaim] The text calls her 'the qedeshah' here, a cult prostitute, in the mouth of Hirah and the men; earlier narrator said zonah (prostitute). I did not model the word choice, only the participants.
[entity:person.tamar.gen_38_6] In the chapter's other events Tamar is AGENT for births (she bears) and PRESENT in the midwife scene; patients are the infants. Reviewer may prefer PATIENT.
